context: Find the derivative of the function \(y = f(x)\) using the derivative of the inverse function \(x = f^{-1}(y)\) in the following
solution:
We first find the inverse of the function \(y = f(x)\), i.e. \(x\) in term of \(y\).
\(y^3 = x + 4\) \(\therefore\) \(x = y^3 - 4\) \(\therefore\) \(x = f^{-1}(y) = y^3 - 4\)
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{\frac{dx}{dy}} = \frac{1}{\frac{d}{dy}\left(y^3 - 4\right)} = \frac{1}{3y^2}\)
\(= \frac{1}{3\left(\sqrt[3]{x + 4}\right)^2} = \frac{1}{3\sqrt[3]{(x + 4)^2}}\) for \(x \neq -4\)

context: Find the derivative of the function \(y = f(x)\) using the derivative of the inverse function \(x = f^{-1}(y)\) in the following
solution:
We first find the inverse of the function \(y = f(x)\), i.e. \(x\) in term of \(y\).
\(y^2 = 1 + \sqrt{x}\) i.e. \(\sqrt{x} = y^2 - 1\), \(\therefore\) \(x = f^{-1}(y) = \left(y^2 - 1\right)^2\)
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{\frac{dx}{dy}} = \frac{1}{\frac{d}{dy}\left[\left(y^2 - 1\right)^2\right]} = \frac{1}{2\left(y^2 - 1\right)\frac{d}{dy}\left(y^2 - 1\right)}\)
\(= \frac{1}{2\left(y^2 - 1\right)(2y)} = \frac{1}{4\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{x}}\left[\left(\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{x}}\right)^2 - 1\right]}\)
\(= \frac{1}{4\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{x}}\left(1 + \sqrt{x} - 1\right)} = \frac{1}{4\sqrt{x}\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{x}}}\)

context: Find the derivative of the function \(y = f(x)\) using the derivative of the inverse function \(x = f^{-1}(y)\) in the following
solution:
We first find the inverse of the function \(y = f(x)\), i.e. \(x\) in term of \(y\).
\(y = \log x\) \(\therefore\) \(x = f^{-1}(y) = e^y\)
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{\frac{dx}{dy}} = \frac{1}{\frac{d}{dy}\left(e^y\right)} = \frac{1}{e^y} = \frac{1}{e^{\ln x}} = \frac{1}{x}\)

stem: Find the derivative of the inverse of function \(y = 2x^3 - 6x\) and calculate its value at \(x = -2\).
solution:
Given : \(y = 2x^3 - 6x\)
Diff. w. r. t. \(x\) we get,
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = 6x^2 - 6 = 6\left(x^2 - 1\right)\)
we have, \(\frac{dx}{dy} = \frac{1}{\frac{dy}{dx}}\)
\(\therefore\) \(\frac{dx}{dy} = \frac{1}{6\left(x^2 - 1\right)}\)
at \(x = -2\),
we get, \(y = 2(-2)^3 - 6(-2) = -16 + 12 = -4\)
\(\left[\frac{dx}{dy}\right]_{y = -4} = \frac{1}{\left[\frac{dy}{dx}\right]_{x = -2}} = \frac{1}{6\left((-2)^2 - 1\right)} = \frac{1}{18}\)

Let \(f\) and \(g\) be the inverse functions of each other. The following table lists a few values of \(f\), \(g\) and \(f'\)

| \(x\) | \(f(x)\) | \(g(x)\) | \(f'(x)\) |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(-4\) | \(2\) | \(1\) | \(\frac{1}{3}\) |
| \(1\) | \(-4\) | \(-2\) | \(4\) |

find \(g'(-4)\).
solution:
In order to find \(g'(-4)\), we should first find an expression for \(g'(x)\) for any input \(x\). Since \(f\) and \(g\) are inverses we can use the following identify which holds for any two diffetentiable inverse functions.
\(g'(x) = \frac{1}{f'[g(x)]}\) ... [check, how?]
... \(\left[\text{Hint} : f[g(x)] = x\right]\)
\(\therefore\) \(g'(-4) = \frac{1}{f'[g(-4)]} = \frac{1}{f'(1)} = \frac{1}{4}\)

Given : \(f(x) = x^5 + 2x - 3\)
Diff. w. r. t. \(x\) we get,
\(f'(x) = 5x^4 + 2\)
Note that \(f(x) = -3\) corresponds to \(x = 0\).
\(\therefore\) \(\left(f^{-1}\right)'(-3) = \frac{1}{f'(0)} = \frac{1}{5(0) + 2} = \frac{1}{2}\)
